President of the Republic

To Honourable Abdul Raheem Abdulla, Speaker of the People's Majlis,

After respectful greetings, I write as follows.

With regard to the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (Optional Protocol), formulated to further strengthen matters relating to protecting the rights afforded to persons with disabilities by the "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities", a treaty ratified by the Maldives on 5 April 2010, to fully implement that treaty, and to establish a mechanism through which member states can be held accountable at the international level, after deliberation at the meeting of the Cabinet held on 20 September 2026, it has been decided that the Maldives should accede to that treaty.

As the said Optional Protocol has been found to be an agreement of a kind under which, as stated in Article 115(o)(1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the citizens of the Maldives do not have to bear any obligation as a result of acceding to that treaty, international treaties entered into by those who exercise executive power in the name of the Maldivian State [?]

2/...

are to be acted upon only after they are submitted to the People's Majlis and approved by that Majlis, and in accordance with what that Majlis decides, as stated in Article 93(a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives; therefore, I request that this matter be submitted to the People's Majlis to obtain the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to accede to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" and to submit an instrument of accession to the depositary of that Protocol, and that the decision of the People's Majlis on this matter be communicated.

A copy of the information paper prepared by the Ministry of Health, Family and Welfare regarding the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" is attached to this letter.

Please accept my respects.

Paper submitted to the People's Majlis for a decision regarding the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities"

1. Title:

Regarding the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities"

2. Matters on which the advice of the People's Majlis is sought:

Requesting the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to accede to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Optional Protocol" or the "Protocol").

3. Executive summary:

The Optional Protocol to the "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" is a protocol formulated with the aim of further strengthening matters relating to protecting the rights afforded to persons with disabilities by the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (the Convention), ratified by the Maldives on 5 April 2010, fully implementing that Convention, and establishing a mechanism through which member states can be held accountable at the international level. Where a right or freedom protected and guaranteed under this Convention has been taken away from a person or a group by a State party to the Convention, it sets out the procedures for submitting a complaint to the "Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" established under Article 34 of the Convention, establishes a specific mechanism for that purpose, and sets out detailed procedures to be followed in that regard.

4. Background to the matter:

4.1 The "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Convention"), an international human rights treaty, is a treaty ratified and joined by the Maldives on 5 April 2010. The Maldives has not entered a reservation to any article of that Convention. (A copy of the Convention is included as Schedule 2 of this paper)

4.2 The Optional Protocol, which sets out a mechanism for submitting complaints to the UN "Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "UN Committee") by or on behalf of a person or group within the jurisdiction of the State when the rights set out in the aforementioned Convention have been lost or taken away, and a mechanism for the UN Committee to conduct inquiries into violations, was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 13 December 2006. That Optional Protocol entered into force on 3 May 2008. (A copy of the Optional Protocol is included as Schedule 1 of this paper)

4.3 Although the Maldives ratified the Convention on 5 April 2010, the Maldives has not acceded to the Optional Protocol. As a result, during reviews of the Maldives under various international human rights mechanisms, the Maldives has received many recommendations to ratify this Optional Protocol as soon as possible. (A summary of the recommendations received from the various mechanisms is included as Schedule 3 of this paper)

5. Core of the matter

• This Optional Protocol is a protocol that establishes 2 (two) important mechanisms for strengthening the implementation of the rights set out in the Convention.

• The first mechanism is the mechanism for submitting a complaint ("individual communications") to the UN Committee where individuals or a group within the jurisdiction of a State that ratifies this Protocol believe that a right of those individuals or that group set out in the Convention has been lost, and where those individuals have exhausted the procedure of recourse to all domestic remedies or completed the legal stages.

• The second mechanism is the mechanism by which the UN Committee may conduct an inquiry where reliable information is received that States which ratify this Protocol are systematically and to a large extent violating the rights set out in the Convention.

• This Protocol sets out the conditions relating to complaints submitted and their admissibility, the principles on how complaints are to be accepted, and follow-up on the recommendations made by the UN Committee. In addition, this Protocol sets out such things as procedural protection [?] for protecting complainants from retaliation.

Accession to the Optional Protocol

• This Optional Protocol is a voluntary protocol. The principles of this Protocol are binding only on States parties that ratify the Protocol. Accordingly, of the 192 (one hundred and ninety-two) States that have so far joined the Convention, 108 (one hundred and eight) States have acceded to this Protocol. Of these,

• Where the complaint is not supported by sufficient evidence, or the matters set out in the complaint are "ill-founded", baseless matters;

• Where the facts set out in the main body of the complaint occurred before the Protocol entered into force for that State (if the facts continued after the Protocol entered into force, the complaint may be accepted).

• Article 4 of the Optional Protocol states that, when the UN Committee receives a complaint under this mechanism, before deciding on the merits of the complaint, the UN Committee may send a request to the State concerned asking that State to take [?] measures to protect the complainant from irreparable harm that may be caused to them.

• When a complaint is submitted to the UN Committee, the Committee shall bring it confidentially to the attention of the State concerned. The State is given 6 (six) months to respond to the complaint. The Committee examines the matter in closed meetings, on the basis of all the information submitted to the Committee.

• After examining the complaint, the Committee's views and recommendations shall be sent to the member State concerned. The member State concerned must respond in writing within 6 (six) months with a reply to the Committee's views and recommendations [?]. Article 7 of the Optional Protocol states that, in so responding, it is requested to share information on any measures taken in relation to the Committee's views and recommendations.

The inquiry mechanism if the Optional Protocol is acceded to

• Under the inquiry mechanism in this Protocol, if reliable information is received that a member State is systematically and to a large extent violating the rights set out in the Convention, the UN Committee is given the power to conduct an inquiry in relation to that information. Article 6(5) of the Optional Protocol states that such an inquiry must be conducted confidentially, and that the cooperation of the State must be sought at all stages of the inquiry.

• If the Committee considers it necessary during the inquiry, it may, with the consent of the member State, arrange to make a visit. On completion of the inquiry, the Committee shall send the findings and recommendations of the inquiry to the State. The State must submit a response within 6 (six) months from the date of receiving the Committee's findings and recommendations.

All [?] of acceding to the Optional Protocol [?]

• Among the objectives that would be achieved by the Maldives accepting and acceding to this Optional Protocol, the matters set out below are noted.

• Further demonstrating the importance the Maldives gives to the rights of persons with disabilities - It demonstrates that the Maldives has a firm commitment to protecting the rights of persons with disabilities. It also strengthens the Government of Maldives' pledge to implement the Convention appropriately and meaningfully.

• Strengthening accountability and access to justice - Individuals are given an additional opportunity, in a way that demonstrates the influence [?] on remedies [?] at the individual level. Through additional protection and seeking remedies [?] [?], public trust in the accountability of the Government of Maldives will increase.

• Advancing transparency - It demonstrates that the Maldives has put itself forward to participate in international scrutiny and [?] reviews. It also shows that the Maldives does not shy away from being accountable within international human rights mechanisms.

• Strengthening the Maldives' position in the international arena - It paves the way for the Maldives to be seen in the international arena as a State that respects international [?] human rights. It also paves the way to increase the Maldives' credibility and standing in international human rights forums.

• In addition, we note that there are mechanisms the Maldives currently adheres to. Among them, as the Maldives has accepted exactly this kind of mechanism under [?] other international human rights treaties, we note that it is already being held accountable under those mechanisms. Among these, we note the work being done [?] on this responsibility. (Information on the mechanisms the Maldives has adhered to so far is included as Schedule 4 of this paper)

6. Parties consulted in relation to the matter:

• Attorney General's Office (Schedule 5)
• Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Schedule 6)
• Cabinet (Schedule 7)

7. Statement of the extent of connection to various matters

• Budgetary impact:

Ratifying this Protocol will not directly incur any additional expenditure for the Government. However, as accepting this Protocol is an agreement with an independent international monitoring mechanism, the Maldives will have to respond in relation to recommendations received under international treaties sent through this mechanism. Also, with regard to a budget for the work to be carried out under the Protocol or the costs incurred in implementation, the responsibilities of accountability and reporting to the UN Committee for the work and measures to be taken in relation to the Committee are considered as costs that will be incurred in connection with the work.

• Legal impact:

Upon the Maldives' accession to this Protocol, the Maldives' legal obligations under this Protocol do not conflict in any way with the Constitution of the Maldives or the Maldives [unclear]. As this Protocol is a treaty of the kind set out in Article 93(a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, it must be ratified in accordance with that article. [?]

• Human rights impact:

Acceding to this Protocol will give additional strength to protecting the rights of persons with disabilities. It will also pave the way for fully implementing the principles of the Convention in the Maldives.

• Section on equality of opportunities for both genders:

We do not believe that the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" will have an adverse impact on gender equality.

• Impact on the environment:

We do not believe that the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" will have an adverse impact on the environment.

• Section on publication and providing information:

No specific special arrangement relating to publication and providing information has been noted in connection with the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities"

• Additional expenditure or action required of the public:

It has not been noted that the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" will require the public to bear any additional expenditure or financial [?].

8. Proposals submitted regarding the matter:

To obtain the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to accede [?] to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities".

Article 13

1. Subject to the entry into force of the Convention, the present Protocol shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the deposit of the tenth instrument of ratification or accession.

2. For each State or regional integration organization ratifying, formally confirming or acceding to the present Protocol after the deposit of the tenth such instrument, the Protocol shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the deposit of its own such instrument.

Article 14

1. Reservations incompatible with the object and purpose of the present Protocol shall not be permitted.

2. Reservations may be withdrawn at any time.

Article 15

1. Any State Party may propose an amendment to the present Protocol and submit it to the Secretary-General of the United Nations. The Secretary-General shall communicate any proposed amendments to States Parties, with a request to be notified whether they favour a meeting of States Parties for the purpose of considering and deciding upon the proposals. In the event that, within four months from the date of such communication, at least one third of the States Parties favour such a meeting, the Secretary-General shall convene the meeting under the auspices of the United Nations. Any amendment adopted by a majority of two thirds of the States Parties present and voting shall be

submitted by the Secretary-General to the General Assembly of the United Nations for approval and thereafter to all States Parties for acceptance.

2. An amendment adopted and approved in accordance with paragraph 1 of this article shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the number of instruments of acceptance deposited reaches two thirds of the number of States Parties at the date of adoption of the amendment. Thereafter, the amendment shall enter into force for any State Party on the thirtieth day following the deposit of its own instrument of acceptance. An amendment shall be binding only on those States Parties which have accepted it.

Article 16

A State Party may denounce the present Protocol by written notification to the Secretary-General of the United Nations. The denunciation shall become effective one year after the date of receipt of the notification by the Secretary-General.

Article 17

The text of the present Protocol shall be made available in accessible formats.

Article 18

The Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts of the present Protocol shall be equally authentic.

Article 40
Conference of States Parties

1. The States Parties shall meet regularly in a Conference of States Parties in order to consider any matter with regard to the implementation of the present Convention.

2. No later than six months after the entry into force of the present Convention, the Conference of States Parties shall be convened by the Secretary-General of the United Nations. The subsequent meetings shall be convened by the Secretary-General biennially or upon the decision of the Conference of States Parties.

Article 41
Depositary

The Secretary-General of the United Nations shall be the depositary of the present Convention.

Article 42
Signature

The present Convention shall be open for signature by all States and by regional integration organizations at United Nations Headquarters in New York as of 30 March 2007.

Article 43
Consent to be bound

The present Convention shall be subject to ratification by signatory States and to formal confirmation by signatory regional integration organizations. It shall be open for accession by any State or regional integration organization which has not signed the Convention.

Article 44
Regional integration organizations

1. "Regional integration organization" shall mean an organization constituted by sovereign States of a given region, to which its member States have transferred competence in respect of matters governed by the present Convention. Such organizations shall declare, in their instruments of formal

confirmation or accession, the extent of their competence with respect to matters governed by the present Convention. Subsequently, they shall inform the depositary of any substantial modification in the extent of their competence.

2. References to "States Parties" in the present Convention shall apply to such organizations within the limits of their competence.

3. For the purposes of article 45, paragraph 1, and article 47, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the present Convention, any instrument deposited by a regional integration organization shall not be counted.

4. Regional integration organizations, in matters within their competence, may exercise their right to vote in the Conference of States Parties, with a number of votes equal to the number of their member States that are Parties to the present Convention. Such an organization shall not exercise its right to vote if any of its member States exercises its right, and vice versa.

Article 45
Entry into force

1. The present Convention shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the deposit of the twentieth instrument of ratification or accession.

2. For each State or regional integration organization ratifying, formally confirming or acceding to the present Convention after the deposit of the twentieth such instrument, the Convention shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the deposit of its own such instrument.

Article 46
Reservations

1. Reservations incompatible with the object and purpose of the present Convention shall not be permitted.

2. Reservations may be withdrawn at any time.

Article 47
Amendments

1. Any State Party may propose an amendment to the present Convention and submit it to the Secretary-General of the United Nations. The Secretary-General shall communicate any proposed amendments to States Parties, with a request to be notified whether they favour a conference of States Parties for the purpose of considering and deciding upon the proposals. In the event that, within four months from the date of such communication, at least one third of

the States Parties favour such a conference, the Secretary-General shall convene the conference under the auspices of the United Nations. Any amendment adopted by a majority of two thirds of the States Parties present and voting shall be submitted by the Secretary-General to the General Assembly of the United Nations for approval and thereafter to all States Parties for acceptance.

2. An amendment adopted and approved in accordance with paragraph 1 of this article shall enter into force on the thirtieth day after the number of instruments of acceptance deposited reaches two thirds of the number of States Parties at the date of adoption of the amendment. Thereafter, the amendment shall enter into force for any State Party on the thirtieth day following the deposit of its own instrument of acceptance. An amendment shall be binding only on those States Parties which have accepted it.

3. If so decided by the Conference of States Parties by consensus, an amendment adopted and approved in accordance with paragraph 1 of this article which relates exclusively to articles 34, 38, 39 and 40 shall enter into force for all States Parties on the thirtieth day after the number of instruments of acceptance deposited reaches two thirds of the number of States Parties at the date of adoption of the amendment.

Article 48
Denunciation

A State Party may denounce the present Convention by written notification to the Secretary-General of the United Nations. The denunciation shall become effective one year after the date of receipt of the notification by the Secretary-General.

Article 49
Accessible format

The text of the present Convention shall be made available in accessible formats.

Article 50
Authentic texts

The Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts of the present Convention shall be equally authentic.

IN WITNESS THEREOF the undersigned plenipotentiaries, being duly authorized thereto by their respective Governments, have signed the present Convention.

Number: 32-LAD/459/2025/58

To Dr Aishath Shiham, Minister of Social and Family Development,

After respectful greetings, I write as follows.

Referring to your Ministry's letter number 459-LA/32/2025/23 (14 August 2025), I write as you have requested this Office's advice regarding the Maldives' accession to the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Optional Protocol" or the "Protocol").

1. It is noted that the said Optional Protocol is a protocol formulated with the aim of further strengthening matters relating to the rights protected for persons with special needs by the "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Convention"), a treaty ratified by the Maldives on 5 August 2010, and of establishing a mechanism for holding member States accountable at the international level in fully implementing that Convention; and accordingly, it is noted that, where a right or freedom whose protection is guaranteed under the said Convention has been taken away from persons or a group by a party to that Convention, it sets out procedures for submitting a matter to the "Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (Committee) established under Article 34 of that Convention, establishes a specific mechanism for that purpose and sets out detailed procedures to be followed in that regard. Accordingly, it is noted that Article 1 of the Protocol states that States acceding to the Protocol accept that the Committee has the competence to receive and consider a communication submitted, through [?] [?] to the Committee, by an individual or groups of a member State of the Convention, stating that member States of the Convention have violated that Convention.

2. Article 2 of the Optional Protocol sets out the communications ("matters") that the Committee must not accept. It is also noted that Articles 3 and 4 of the Protocol set out the procedures relating to accepting matters submitted to the Committee and sharing them with the member State, the interim measures to be taken before accepting such matters, or the decisions and recommendations, and the procedures for the actions the Committee considers appropriate on the matters and recommendations it makes, and for how the person who submitted the matter (petitioner) is to be informed.

3. In addition, with regard to Articles 6 and 7 of the Protocol, it is particularly noted that they set out the procedures for how an inquiry is to be conducted where the Committee receives information indicating that a systematic violation or serious violation is being committed contrary to the rights set out in the Convention. It is also noted that, with regard to Article 8 of the Protocol, it is stated that a declaration may be made when signing or ratifying the Protocol that, while being a party, it does not recognise the competence of the Committee to consider matters as set out in Articles 6 and 7 as stated above.

4. In addition to the matters noted so far in relation to the Protocol, it is noted that the procedures set out in that Protocol, the procedures for withdrawing from that Protocol, and matters relating to making reservations to the Protocol are set out from Article 9 to Article 16 of that Protocol. Accordingly;

4.1 Looking at Article 10 of the Protocol, it is noted that the Protocol has been open for signature by States from 30 March 2007. Also, looking at Article 11 of the Protocol, it is noted that this Protocol is a protocol that must be ratified in addition to being signed, and further, that the opportunity has been opened for States that have not signed the Protocol so far, but have ratified the Convention, to "accede" to the Protocol.

4.2 It is noted that Article 13 of the Protocol provides that, once 10 instruments of ratification or accession have been deposited for participation in the Protocol, the Protocol shall enter into force [unclear] on the date on which 30 days have passed from the date of deposit of the 10th instrument of ratification or accession.
